To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the lytic action of lysozyme on bacterial cells is inhibited by cardiotoxin II, a polypeptide toxin from the venom of the Indian coba Naja naja, and that the inhibition of lysozymic action by cardiotoxin is similar to that by antibiotics such as thiostrepton and polymyxin.
cardiotoxin II exes a powerful, but complete, and reversible, inhibitory action of the lysis of the killed cell of micrococcus by lysozymes.
cardiotoxin II, thiostrepton and polymyxin inhibit lysozyme induced lysis of killed Micrococcus lysodiketicus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the action of lytic enzymes and antibiotics.
the inhibition of lysozyme activity by certain antibiotics.

the inhibitory action of cardiotoxin, a polypeptide from the venom of Naja naja (Indian cobra), on the action of lysozyme, and the inhibitory action on this lysozyme activity of certain antibiotics, which have a similar structure to the cardiotoxin.

the inhibition of the lysis of M. lysodeikticos by cardiotoxin II, thiostrepton or polymyxin B is due to the formation of a complex of the antibiotic with the cell membrane, which is then not accessible to lysozyme.

the inhibitory action of cardiotoxin is not related to the antibacterial properties of the compounds tested, but to the presence of a certain structural element, which is common to all compounds tested.

the inhibitory action of cardiotoxin on the lytic activity of lysozyme and of the antibiotics on the inhibitory action by cardiotoxin is due to the binding of the inhibitor to the substrate and not to the lysozyme.

the inhibition of the action of lysozyme by cardiotoxin II is not a specific phenomenon, but is due to an interaction between the lysozyme and a basic protein or peptide.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the lytic effect of lysozyme is inhibited in a manner that is independent of the nature of the cell-wall component attacked, the chemical nature of the lytic agent or the nature of the antibiotic.
the inhibitory action on lysis by the above antibiotics is not related to their antibacterial action, but is due to a specific interaction with the enzyme lysozyme.
the inhibition of the lytic action of lysozyme is not a general phenomenon of all antibiotics.
